selected_question: Can the current exact-execution effect-authority candidate rely on a physically singleton FrankExecutionGate, and does the directory-FD repair remain singleton when the lock marker or the entire state-root pathname is replaced?

mechanisms: exact V16 execution_id + credential + admitted ingress identity
B1 reservation / B2 attempt / B3 provider-precommit fence
known_remaining_gates: integration with replacement-safe physical singleton Gate

physical_gate_negative_lane.meaning: Locking a replaceable lockfile pathname is insufficient physical singleton evidence because a live holder retains the old open-file-description lock while a contender can open and lock a newly materialized inode.

physical_gate_repair_lane.mechanism: flock an open state-directory FD and verify FD-to-path device/inode identity on acquire, heartbeat and release

initial_run_adjudication.cause: Immediate unlink/recreate on ext4 reused the just-freed marker inode number, so the test incorrectly assumed path replacement always implies a numerically different inode.

test_only_fix.change: Keep an unflocked descriptor to the pre-intervention marker open across unlink/recreate so inode-number recycling cannot alias the old and replacement directory entries; compare replacement path identity to the preserved old open-FD identity.

external_primary_evidence.source: etcd documentation — etcd versus other key-value stores
external_primary_evidence.design_implication: Lease/lock state by itself is not sufficient protection for external resources; downstream effect boundaries need generation/version validation.

external_primary_evidence.source: Burrows, The Chubby lock service, OSDI 2006
external_primary_evidence.design_implication: A sequencer/generation validated by the receiving service prevents stale lock holders from acting as current.
flock locks are associated with open file descriptions; pathname replacement is not equivalent to replacing a live open-file-description lock.

rename leaves existing open file descriptors unaffected and requires write/search permissions at the containing-directory boundary; parent-directory permissions can therefore become an explicit deployment fence against state-root replacement.

exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.intervention: While holder A retains the repaired state-directory FD/flock, rename the entire disposable state-root pathname away, materialize a fresh migrated state root at the original path, let contender B enter the real repaired Gate, then force A through its next anchor path-identity heartbeat check.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.hypothesis: Directory-FD locking closes marker-file replacement but cannot by itself prevent a replacement state-root pathname from creating a second independent physical and semantic generation before the old holder reaches its next path-identity check.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.strongest_counterhypothesis: Production ownership/mount policy makes state-root rename/replacement unreachable to Frank and all allowed tools; if measured true, an explicit deployment invariant can close this class without another runtime lock architecture.

hypothesis_matrix.claim: A state-directory open-FD flock plus FD/path identity checks closes the already-measured lockfile-entry unlink/recreate split-brain class.
hypothesis_matrix.falsifier: Corrected PR #225 target regression still admits a contender while A holds the original directory FD, or breaks the unchanged execution-gate recovery/exclusion baseline.

hypothesis_matrix.claim: The first PR #225 target failure was a product-runtime failure rather than a discriminator artifact.
hypothesis_matrix.evidence: The unchanged baseline passed and the repair test aborted solely on same inode-number reuse before attempting the contender Gate.

hypothesis_matrix.claim: The whole state-root pathname remains a higher-order physical singleton dependency above the directory-FD repair.
hypothesis_matrix.falsifier: PR #235 target run demonstrates the replacement root cannot admit a second Gate, or accepted production deployment independently proves state-root replacement inaccessible before runtime.

hypothesis_matrix.claim: Runtime changes are unnecessary because deployment permissions alone can make state-root replacement impossible.
hypothesis_matrix.next_test: If #235 reproduces on disposable state, inspect and harden accepted target parent-directory ownership/mode/mount/service sandbox, then rerun a same-UID rename denial plus normal in-state write/recovery matrix.

architecture_delta.candidate_simplification_if_oob_reproduc: Prefer a root/deployment-owned non-renamable parent boundary for the state root, while retaining write access inside the state root, if target measurements prove it sufficient. Do not add a third semantic lease authority merely to compensate for filesystem permissions that can be made explicit and testable.
architecture_delta.effect_on_pr228: PR #228 can prove exact issuance by its Gate but cannot yet prove that Gate is the sole possible global current Gate until the #225/#235 physical-singleton dependency is closed.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product architecture was promoted by this run; the PR #225 change remains draft and the PR #235 branch is diagnostic-only.
